html:
SMTO-CFG-0104 — Some SMTO website pages failed their publishing checks

GUID: 934db058-e268-53b6-bcfb-7774bac71f8f
Slug: public-site-content-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: public

What happened

  • A page, picture or link on the public SMTO website didn't pass the checks run before publishing, for example a broken link or a file that's missing or too large. The website can't start until it's fixed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Read the message. It usually names the page and its source file, for example a broken link on a page or a missing source file. Knowing the exact page tells you where to make the fix.
  2. Fix that item: correct or remove the broken link, add the missing file, or shorten a page or picture that's too large. Pages must stay within size limits and only link to pages that exist.
  3. If the message says files changed during startup, wait for any copy or build to finish, then start the website again. The website refuses files that change while it's loading them.
  4. From the SMTO folder, run python scripts/validate-smto-site-content.py and publish only when it finishes without an error. The check runs the same tests the website runs when it starts.

What success looks like

  • The check finishes without an error, and the website starts.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message and send it to the person who maintains the website content. Don't delete publishing records, and don't repeat a publish whose result you're unsure of; look at the live site first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Public website content validation failed: an unsafe, missing, symlinked or oversized source, mismatched publication metadata or frontmatter, an invalid or duplicate route or status, a broken internal link or heading fragment, changed static fingerprints, or an exceeded page or asset budget.

What this means

  • Public content/asset loading or validation finds unsafe/missing/oversized sources, stale fingerprints/schema/branding, invalid metadata, broken links/fragments or exceeded page/asset budgets. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Public content/asset loading or validation finds unsafe/missing/oversized sources, stale fingerprints/schema/branding, invalid metadata, broken links/fragments or exceeded page/asset budgets.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact source, route or asset named by validation; correct the failed check without silently publishing partial content.

How to fix it

  • Use the route and source named in the error to fix src/smto_site/content/public_docs.json, the Markdown source or the static asset (sources at most 512,000 bytes, no symlinks or traversal, frontmatter matching the publication entry, valid internal links and anchors). Rebuild with scripts/build-smto-site.py if assets changed, and run python scripts/validate-smto-site-content.py before publishing.
  • Correct the reported public source, metadata or asset and run the site validation command before publishing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The complete supported site validation passes with intended content and assets.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
